question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y-4z &=8 \\ -x+3y+7z &=-10.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & 7 & -10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & 7 & -10\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -2\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2z &=4 \\ y+3z &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2z+4 \\ y &=-3z-2 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2z+4 \\ -3z-2 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-6y &=9 \\  -2x+4y &=-6 \\  x-2y &=3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2y+3 \\  y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2y+3 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
